walkthroughs.body_html:
Voice of the Genome — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Voice of the Genome brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Voice of the Genome.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why is ATP described as an 'energy currency' rather than energy storage?
options: ATP is permanent and accumulates with age in cells.
ATP is constantly made and broken down — it transfers energy between reactions rather than storing large amounts for later.
Cells store large amounts of ATP for emergency use.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Plants only respire at night and only photosynthesise during the day; the processes never overlap.
Plants only photosynthesise and do not respire; respiration is for animals only.
Yes — plants respire all the time to release energy; they also photosynthesise when there is light.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the guide RNA in CRISPR-Cas9?
options: Guide RNA is the enzyme that cuts the DNA.
Guide RNA is the new sequence that gets inserted into the genome.
ATP is permanent and accumulates with age in cells.
It directs Cas9 to the specific DNA sequence to cut by base-pairing with the target.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Monomer”?
options: Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Polymer”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Ester bond”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Condensation reaction”?
options: Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrolysis”?
options: Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Small repeating subunit that forms polymers, e.g. amino acid, monosaccharide, nucleotide.
Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Large molecule formed from many monomers joined by condensation reactions.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glycosidic bond”?
options: Covalent bond between two sugar molecules formed by condensation.
Breaking of a bond by addition of water; reverse of condensation.
Bond between glycerol and a fatty acid in triglycerides, formed by condensation.
Joining of two molecules with loss of water and formation of a new chemical bond.
